turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I volunteered to cook for twenty people at the community hall. My recipe serves four. Moshi, do I just times it by five?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Mostly yes for the main ingredients. Be careful with salt and spices though, scale those up a bit less and taste as you go.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Strong flavors don't always scale evenly, and you can always add more. Taking it out is the hard part.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Makes sense. It's a beef stew. Will it take five times longer?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: No, but a much bigger pot will take longer to come to a simmer. Allow an extra hour or so.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don't even own a pot that big.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ask the hall, they often have catering pots. Otherwise split it between two or three pans.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good idea, I'll call them. I'm a bit nervous, honestly

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've never cooked for a crowd.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Stew is a kind dish to start with. It reheats well, it's better the next day, and nobody minds seconds.
